content: The study evaluated the outcomes of leprosy treatment using Uniform Multidrug Therapy (U-MDT) and Regular Multidrug Therapy (R-MDT) in both paucibacillary (PB) and multibacillary (MB) patients. The following findings were observed: 1. Bacilloscopic Index (BI) Reduction: The average decrease in the bacilloscopic index was reported for both U-MDT and R-MDT groups. However, specific statistical analyses were not performed due to the small sample sizes. 2. Histopathological Improvement in PB Patients: At 6 months, 91% of U-MDT patients showed good or reversal reactions, while 9% showed no change or poor outcomes. In the R-MDT group, 80% showed good or reversal reactions, and 20% showed no change or poor outcomes. At 12 months, 100% of U-MDT patients showed good or reversal reactions, with none showing poor outcomes. In the R-MDT group, 86% showed good or reversal reactions, and 14% showed no change or poor outcomes. At 18 months, 83% of U-MDT patients showed good or reversal reactions, with none showing poor outcomes. In the R-MDT group, 100% showed good or reversal reactions. At 24 months, 100% of U-MDT patients showed good or reversal reactions. In the R-MDT group, 67% showed good or reversal reactions, and 33% showed no change or poor outcomes. 3. Histopathological Improvement in MB Patients: At 12 months, 100% of U-MDT patients showed good or reversal reactions, with none showing poor outcomes. In the R-MDT group, 77% showed good or reversal reactions, and 23% showed no change or poor outcomes. At 18 months, 50% of U-MDT patients showed good or reversal reactions, while 50% showed no change or poor outcomes. In the R-MDT group, 100% showed good or reversal reactions. At 24 months, 100% of R-MDT patients showed good or reversal reactions, with none showing poor outcomes. Data for U-MDT patients at this time point were not available. 4. Adverse Effects: Among PB patients, two developed dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome, and one developed acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP). These adverse effects occurred within the first 4 weeks of therapy. Clofazimine pigmentation was observed in 11 patients (2 PB and 9 MB), which regressed over 9 months. 5. Follow-Up and Dropout Rates: Of the 64 patients initially enrolled, 87% were available for biopsy at entry, 45% at 12 months, 21% at 18 months, and 10% at 24 months. The dropout rate at the end of the study varied, and detailed reasons for losses to follow-up were not consistently reported. 6. Study Design and Limitations: The study included both clinical trials and cohort studies, with varying durations of follow-up (up to 24 months). Statistical analyses were limited due to small sample sizes, and some outcomes were not clearly defined or reported. The quality of the studies was rated as fair, with limitations in randomization, blinding, and reporting of outcomes. 7. Tolerability of Therapy: Overall, the therapy was well-tolerated. However, pigmentation due to clofazimine and hypersensitivity reactions to dapsone were noted as significant side effects. 8. Research Objectives and Population: The studies aimed to evaluate the clinical and histological benefits of U-MDT compared to R-MDT in leprosy patients. The study populations were clearly defined, but participation rates and sample size justifications were not consistently provided. In conclusion, U-MDT demonstrated comparable or slightly better outcomes in terms of histopathological improvement and tolerability compared to R-MDT, though the small sample sizes and methodological limitations restrict the generalizability of the findings.
